messages:
Tess: hi all :wave: day 2 onboarding question — building runtime from source on an Ubuntu 22.04 dev VM. used CUDA 13.1 runfile but skipped the bundled driver. build fails at link with undefined refs to cuInit/cuDeviceGet. `ldd build/bin/runtime` shows `libcuda.so.1 => not found`. any quick checks?
Mika: welcome! :tada: sounds like the driver library isn't visible to the loader. can you paste `nvidia-smi` and the last 8 lines of the linker error?
Tess: nvidia-smi shows Driver 535.113 / CUDA 13.1. linker snippet:
```
/usr/bin/ld: build/liblibruntime.a(cuda_driver.o): in function `InitDriver':
cuda_driver.cpp:(.text+0x1a7): undefined reference to `cuInit'
collect2: error: ld returned 1 exit status
```
Tess: also `ldd build/bin/runtime` yields `libcuda.so.1 => not found`, but I have `/usr/local/cuda-13/lib64/libcuda.so.1` from the runfile.
Samir: runfile toolkits sometimes drop the kernel driver lib in a non-standard place. check `/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1` and `dpkg -l | grep nvidia`. If the real driver isn't installed, apt-install `nvidia-driver-535`.
Rosie: quick temporary hack: export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/local/cuda-13/lib64:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH and rebuild — that'll help link, but prefer installing the distro driver and running `sudo ldconfig`.
Tess: apt installed `nvidia-driver-535` + ldconfig. now ldd resolves `libcuda.so.1 => /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1`. re-run build and hit `ptxas: error: Illegal instruction` coming from `/usr/local/cuda-13/bin/ptxas`. CI (buildkite) fails on kernel compile step.
buildkite: [ci/runtime-build #214] failed — step compile-kernels exited 1. tail: `ptxas: info : 64-bit ELF : /usr/local/cuda-13/bin/ptxas
ptxas: error: Illegal instruction`
Mika: `Illegal instruction` usually means ptxas uses CPU instrs not available on the VM host (AVX512/AVX2 mismatch). what's `lscpu` or `cat /proc/cpuinfo` say?
Tess: the VM is older Skylake, no AVX512. `file /usr/local/cuda-13/bin/ptxas` shows ELF 64-bit. executing ptxas locally crashes with SIGILL.
Samir: NV distributes ptxas built for newer microarchitectures in some toolkits. Option A: use NVIDIA's CUDA container (nvcr.io/nvidia/cuda:13.1-devel-ubuntu22.04) to build — container runtime has compatible userland. Option B: install the toolkit from the distro package (apt) which often contains a compatible ptxas for older CPUs. Option C: use a newer VM with required CPU features.
Rosie: also avoid copying toolkit `libcuda` into system lib dirs — that causes ABI/kernel mismatches. If you go with the container route, mount your repo and bind the host driver: `docker run --gpus all -v $PWD:/src -w /src nvcr.io/nvidia/cuda:13.1-devel-ubuntu22.04 bash` then cmake/build inside.
Tess: tried the container approach — built inside the cuda:13.1-devel image, ptxas runs fine, and the build completed. :white_check_mark:
Mika: excellent. we'll add this to onboarding notes: always check that `libcuda.so.1` comes from the kernel driver (look under /usr/lib...), prefer distro driver packages, and use the NVIDIA container if ptxas SIGILL occurs.
Samir: I'll add a short checklist to the eng-runtime onboarding doc: 1) verify `nvidia-smi`, 2) ensure `/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1` exists, 3) prefer apt `nvidia-driver-535`, 4) if `ptxas` illegal instr, build in official CUDA container or use matching toolkit package.
Tess: thanks for the help — saved my afternoon :clap:
